rationale: The article contrasts two distinct paradigms for snow removal: the expensive, high-capacity electrical footprint of a heated mat versus the dense, low-cost mechanical energy of a battery blower. A split-screen cinematic still allows a side-by-side comparison of the physical footprints on a driveway slab under dramatic dusk lighting.
subject: A heated driveway mat and a snow blower battery pack
core_thesis: A heated snow mat's true cost is measured per square foot of hardware and circuit capacity, making it vastly more expensive than a battery blower for large areas like a driveway.
core_conflict: Latent-heat work (melting snow via resistance heating) versus mechanical work (throwing snow via a battery motor) across a fixed area of pavement.
